properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js supplies the hash primitives inside elliptic's secp256k1 stack that ethers v5 tooling uses in this Hardhat example. No direct call site in the repo's own source; the package ships the algorithms.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA is the signature scheme every Ethereum EOA transaction uses; the ethers-v5 contract-verification example targets chains where the algorithm is protocol-fixed (observable here, replaceable only by a chain-level change), while the dependency pin is changeable in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: the shipped dependency set contains Ed25519 signatures; the example's scripts drive contract verification via ethers v5 rather than Ed25519 directly. Replaceable by a dependency bump here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is ethers v5's signing engine: any Wallet.sendTransaction / signMessage the example performs goes through it. Its secp256k1 ECDSA is dictated by the Ethereum protocol; the pin is changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is the EC library of the Hardhat/ethers example tree (pulled via @scure/bip32 HD-wallet code paths). Ships P-256, secp256k1, ed25519, x25519; only the P-256 algorithm view was collected.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH engine behind ethers v5 signing and the hardhat/ethereumjs toolchain in this example. The ECDH path is a real capability of the shipped package even where only ECDSA is exercised.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: X25519 arrives via tweetnacl with no application call site observed; the hardhat/ethers toolchain pulls it in transitively.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ethers v5 wallet encryption (Wallet.encrypt / JSON keystore) uses PBKDF2/scrypt to derive keystore keys; the example imports ethers, so this KDF ships in its dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the hash library of the Hardhat/ethers example tree (SHA-2/SHA-3/Keccak/BLAKE2/BLAKE3/RIPEMD-160). SHA-256 itself is Grover-resistant (quantum-safe class), so this is a posture baseline entry rather than a migration item.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: hash algorithms from @noble/hashes are present in the shipped dependency tree even though the example's own scripts don't call BLAKE3 directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the scrypt KDF ethers v5 uses to encrypt keystore JSON wallets (json-wallets). Password KDF, quantum-safe class; the parameters that matter (N/r/p) live inside the library, not in this repo's source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset; keccak256 (SHA-3 family) is also central to Ethereum hashing more broadly, so the family ships in the dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: tweetnacl's authenticated-encryption surface ships with the build; the example's contract-verification scripts do not call it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl ships X25519 (Shor-vulnerable KEX), Ed25519 (Shor-vulnerable signatures), XSalsa20-Poly1305 (AE, quantum-OK) and SHA-512, reachable through @metamask/eth-sig-util in the Hardhat example tree. No direct call site in this repo's source; the package ships the algorithms.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the KDF behind ethers v5's encrypted-JSON-keystore support, so it ships with the example's node_modules; replaceable by dependency management here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js is the browserify SHA-1/SHA-2 implementation pulled in via create-hash/create-hmac/pbkdf2 (crypto-browserify stack). Ships SHA-1 (weak hash) alongside SHA-2. Distinct package from hash.js (ALG-50e53f84/LIB-e966a74e).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the library face of the ECDSA asset (ALG-710f61f0): the pin matters because elliptic 6.5.x carries known supply-chain advisories (e.g. insufficient input validation) alongside its Shor-vulnerable curve.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: the library's hash surface (SHA-3, BLAKE3, keccak, etc.) ships whether or not the example calls it; version pinned, changeable by dependency bump.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: hash.js ships in the example's dependency tree as elliptic's companion hash/DRBG layer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is the EC library of the example tree; algorithm views (P-256, ed25519, x25519, secp256k1) all hang off this one package entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library face of the PBKDF2 asset (ALG-4de3b020): the node package that performs the KDF inside ethers v5 keystore encryption.
